CVE-2026-123633 (HTTP/2) and CVE-2026-121810 (HTTP/3) are use-after-free bugs in connection draining with proxying to a backend. CVE-2026-123634 is a resolver use-after-free needing a request-derived proxy_pass target plus SSI or mirror subrequests. CVE-2026-113425 hits the mail proxy when proxy and auth_http are combined.

- Root chain: code execution lands as the NGINX worker, then a separate Linux kernel SCTP use-after-free or double free (code introduced in Linux 4.15) escalates to root. The researchers say the chain also crossed a Docker container boundary. That kernel bug has no CVE and no fix yet. ATT&CK per the report: T1190, T1068, T1611.

- Exploit reality: the public PoC for CVE-2026-123007 (GitHub, November 18) gets code execution against NGINX 1.31.8 with HTTP/2 over TLS in a Docker lab. It needs x86-64 with AVX-512 and a particular glibc memory-copy routine, has to defeat ASLR, and pushes roughly 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic down a single connection. A proxy terminating HTTP/2 in front of NGINX will most likely stop it. The discoverers and another team hold working exploits but withheld the final steps. Fake exploit repos are circulating, so vet anything you pull.

The warning signs come from CIRCL's advisory; the grep is from the report's checks.

Run nginx -T 2>/dev/null | grep -nE 'http2|http3|quic|resolver|proxy_pass|mirror|ssi on|auth_http' to see which flaws apply. Check bundled NGINX in container images, appliances and load balancers. Community ingress-nginx is retired with no fix planned. After upgrading, do a full restart, because a reload keeps the old binary running.

If patching waits, disable the feature behind each flaw. Turning off HTTP/2 covers only CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, and disabling mirror alone leaves CVE-2026-123634 open. On hosts that do not need SCTP, add install sctp /bin/false under /etc/modprobe.d/ and confirm with lsmod, since an already-loaded module stays active until reboot or removal. Check sysctl kernel.randomize_va_space (2 is full) and look for services launched with setarch -R. Preserve error logs and worker core dumps before restarting.

Researchers observed that low-privilege database accounts — granted only temporary table rights — can trigger memory-corruption bugs in PostgreSQL, MySQL, and ClickHouse engine code to achieve full OS-level RCE. The Oracle chain (CVE-2026-114819, CVSS 9.9) requires no credentials at all. SQL permission boundaries do not constrain memory-unsafe execution paths — the blast radius begins at the database tier and extends outward from there. Runtime segmentation restricting east-west traffic from database hosts helps contain post-compromise lateral movement before it reaches adjacent services.

#CloudSecurity #ZeroTrust

🔗 Full TRC analysis: https://t.co/nTx00Kc0xI

A database user with almost no permissions can potentially turn a SQL connection into a shell on the server

Security researcher Zheng Yu demonstrated this against PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, and found a separate attack chain against Oracle

The research exposes a gap between database permissions and the code those permissions allow users to reach

Even when an account cannot access application tables, it can still interact with components such as query optimizers, aggregate functions and binary data parsers

A memory corruption flaw in one of those components can turn limited SQL access into operating-system command execution

The demonstrations included:

PostgreSQL — CVE-2026-116331

A type-confusion bug in the query planner allows a default login role to construct objects in its temporary schema and eventually execute commands as the PostgreSQL service account

MySQL — CVE-2026-101786

An out-of-bounds write in windowed BIT_OR aggregation can be triggered using prepared statements and oversized binary input

Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns Serial No and Batch ledger entries without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users without roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to obtain item codes, quantities, warehouses, batch and serial numbers.

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows non-admin users with settings:edit permission to modify OIDC provider configuration due to an improper permission check. Attackers can send a PUT request to /api/auth/oidc/<provider-id> setting adminClaim to their own OIDC group, gaining full admin access on their next OIDC login.

Frappe ERPNext 16.0.0 before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Manufacturing module endpoint that allows authenticated users to cancel Stock Reservation Entries without record-level write permission. Low-privilege attackers can send crafted requests naming manufacturing documents of other companies or outside their User Permissions to release reserved stock and disrupt stock allocation.

web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.10, 4.0.x before 4.0.7, and 4.1.x before 4.1.7 contain a padding oracle in RSACrypt::decryptWithRSA15() because RSA1 5 decryption lacks implicit rejection, so invalid padding, wrong CEK length, and valid padding take measurably different time. Remote attackers can submit adaptively crafted JWE encrypted key values and measure these timing differences to recover the wrapped content encryption key.

Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Projects module endpoint that returns employee costing and billing rates without record-level permission checks. Authenticated users, including portal users or users without roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read other employees' activity cost rates.

Frappe ERPNext 8.0.0 before 15.123.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that allows authenticated users to read restricted warehouse data. Attackers with a common operational role can send crafted requests naming warehouses excluded by their User Permissions to obtain stock quantities and stock values.

Frappe ERPNext 16.0.1 before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock dashboard chart endpoint that returns site-wide stock value when the caller has no permitted warehouse. Authenticated users with common operational roles can send crafted requests naming records outside their scope to read stock value data beyond their permissions.

Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.122.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that allows authenticated users to read Taxes and Charges Template rows without permission checks. Attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read account heads and tax rates.

Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.121.4 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read POS Profile cashier lists by calling a POS endpoint lacking record permission checks. Attackers, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope POS Profiles to retrieve their cashier data.

Frappe ERPNext 12.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns the parsed content of private import-format files without checking permission on the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users without roles, can send crafted requests naming records outside their permitted scope to read those private files.

Frappe ERPNext 7.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in endpoints that build part of a query from caller-supplied sort parameters without validation. Authenticated low-privilege users can send crafted requests whose sort parameter holds SQL that the database executes as part of the query, extracting sensitive information.

Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Selling module endpoint that returns customer loyalty point balances without checking the caller's permission on the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming records outside their permitted scope to read other customers' loyalty point balances.

Frappe ERPNext 15.55.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns a company's Chart of Accounts without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated users, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read any company's Chart of Accounts.

Frappe ERPNext before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a CRM and Support module endpoint that returns Communications of documents without checking whether the caller may read them. Authenticated attackers with a common operational role can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read their email communications and relink them away from their original documents.

Finsys Dockhand 1.0.7 before 1.0.57 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows low-privileged users to read and write arbitrary files by setting an unvalidated envPath on a stack source. Attackers with stacks:edit permission can point envPath to files like /etc/shadow or SSH keys, then use GET or PUT on /api/stacks/[name]/env/raw to read or overwrite them.

Frappe ERPNext 13.49.0 before 14.0.0, 14.17.2 before 15.124.0, and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Selling module endpoint that returns Sales Order line items without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope Sales Orders to read their line item data.

Frappe ERPNext before 15.124.2 and 16.x before 16.53.0 fails to enforce record-level authorization in several endpoints, reports and forms, allowing authenticated low-privilege users to access data beyond their role. Attackers can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read other companies' financial, stock, pricing and contact data or make constrained changes to those records.

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a clickjacking vulnerability because src/hooks.server.ts never sets X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors headers on responses. Attackers on a same-site origin can embed the UI in an invisible iframe to trick authenticated users into stopping stacks, deleting resources, or changing settings.

Web-Token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.10, 4.0.0 before 4.0.7, and 4.1.0 before 4.1.7 contain an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in PBES2AESKW::unwrapKey(), which passes the attacker-controlled p2c JWE header value to hash pbkdf2() without an upper bound. Unauthenticated attackers can send a JWE using a PBES2-HS*+A*KW algorithm with a huge p2c iteration count to force lengthy PBKDF2 computations and exhaust server CPU.

Frappe ERPNext 8.2.5 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns on-hand stock quantities without checking record-level permissions. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users without roles, can send crafted requests naming restricted records to disclose stock quantities and confirm item existence.

Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns uploaded bank statement file content without checking record-level permissions. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming records outside their scope to read full statement file contents.

Vikunja from 0.8.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated project readers to amplify response size by repeating requested properties in CalDAV PROPFIND requests. Attackers can send PROPFIND requests to the dav projects endpoint with hundreds of duplicate calendar-data properties to exhaust server memory, CPU, and bandwidth.

ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the Redis protocol handler, which neither replies to nor closes a pre-authentication connection when it receives an array whose first element is not a string. Unauthenticated attackers can resend such an array just within the 30-second socket idle timeout to hold connections open indefinitely and exhaust RedisNetworkExecutor threads.

Vikunja from 2.6.0 before 2.8.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the Planka migration converter that multiplies task allocations for duplicate list IDs. Attackers controlling a Planka server can return boards with duplicate list IDs and many cards to exhaust memory and OOM-kill the Vikunja process.

OpenRemote from 1.2.0 before 1.34.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in AlarmFacade that allows restricted users with write:rules to create alarms for assets outside their ruleset subtree. Attackers can deploy a JSON asset-scoped ruleset using target.custom asset ids to create HIGH severity alarms and trigger operator notifications about arbitrary in-realm assets.

ArcadeDB 21.10.1 before 26.11.1 contains a resource-limit bypass vulnerability that allows restricted users to evade per-group readTimeout because limits are applied to shared cached statements and plans. Attackers can run SQL text previously cached by an unrestricted principal to skip timeouts, or impose their own timeout and limit on root and other users.

ArcadeDB from 26.7.1 before 26.11.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because LSMTreeFullTextIndex computes BM25 corpus statistics over all buckets of the indexed type, ignoring bucket access control on subtypes. Authenticated users with read access to a supertype but not its subtype can run EXPLAIN or PROFILE on full-text queries and read totalDocs and per-term df values to count hidden subtype documents containing chosen terms.

SurrealDB from 3.2.0 before 3.3.4 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows record users to update protected rows by exploiting table-level PERMISSIONS FOR update predicates referencing COMPUTED fields. Because check update permissions evaluates the predicate before computed fields are populated, the field reads as NONE and deny-intended predicates like blocked != true pass, letting attackers modify records.

better-auth 1.3.0 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the admin plugin's /admin/update-user endpoint that lets roles holding user:update change another user's phoneNumber and phoneNumberVerified fields. Attackers can set their own verified phone number on a higher-privileged account and sign in via phone OTP to take it over.

Vikunja from 1.0.0 before 2.8.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows attackers to hijack SSO identities by planting local accounts with unverified victim emails. When emailfallback is enabled, attackers register or edit a local account using the victim's email, causing the victim's first OIDC login to link into the attacker-controlled account and expose their data.

Better Auth (better-auth, @better-auth/kysely-adapter, and @better-auth/drizzle-adapter) before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a race condition with MySQL or MariaDB serial IDs because the inserted row's ID is read via a separate LAST INSERT ID() query that may run on a different pooled connection. Under concurrent load, a user signing in can receive another user's session and act as that user.

Frappe ERPNext 14.47.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Accounts module where a method on accounting vouchers creates and submits Repost Accounting Ledger documents with permission checks skipped. Authenticated users with read access to a Sales Invoice, Purchase Invoice, Payment Entry, Journal Entry, or Purchase Receipt can call it to delete and repost that voucher's General Ledger entries, an action restricted to System Managers.

Frappe ERPNext 7.1.0 before 15.121.0 and 16.x before 16.34.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Projects module endpoints that return Timesheet data without restricting results to records the caller may read. Any authenticated user, including one with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests to read organisation-wide Timesheet work and billing details.

rclone before 1.76.0 leaks credentials in its swift, netstorage and seafile backends, which follow HTTP redirects using Go's default policy: swift and netstorage send auth headers or passwords on cross-host or HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects, and seafile sends API tokens or passwords on same-host HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects. Attackers receiving or observing a redirect issued by the configured endpoint can capture these credentials to access storage or replay signed requests.

ArcadeDB from 26.11.1-SNAPSHOT before 26.11.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to skip per-type ACL checks when a database is opened on demand. Attackers can send the first POST /api/v1/batch/{database} request to a closed database to read and write types they are not entitled to access.

Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in a Selling module endpoint that checks only document-type write permission, not permission on each Sales Order, when closing or reopening Sales Orders. Authenticated users restricted by User Permissions can send crafted requests naming another company's Sales Order to close or reopen it outside their restriction.

Frappe ERPNext 15.111.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.22.0 before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns item rows of a caller-named inter-company invoice or order and accepts a caller-supplied document type without checking read permission. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming another company's document to read Sales Invoice, Purchase Invoice and order items.

Frappe ERPNext 4.3.0 before 15.121.6 and 16.x before 16.37.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in an endpoint of the Selling and Buying modules, where a request value validated early can be overridden by caller-supplied data that reaches a database query unvalidated. Any authenticated user, including a portal user with no roles, can send crafted requests to extract sensitive data, including active session data, and take over other accounts such as administrators.

ArcadeDB 25.8.1 before 26.11.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability because per-type ACLs are keyed by type name, renames are not propagated to the permission configuration, and requestAccessOnType allows unknown type names by default. Authenticated users holding only updateSchema can run ALTER TYPE NAME on a denied type to gain read, DELETE and TRUNCATE access, immediately for TIMESERIES types and after the next security rebuild for record-backed types.

AzuraCast 0.19.0 before 0.24.1 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows users with station media rights to add tracks to other stations' playlists by supplying foreign playlist ids to the single-file edit endpoint. Attackers can send sequential playlist ids in the playlists array to inject entries into other stations' AutoDJ rotations and public now-playing metadata, causing failed playback slots.

Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.34.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns the subscription plans linked to a caller-named invoice without checking read permission on that invoice. Authenticated attackers can send crafted requests naming invoices outside their permitted scope to learn whether they belong to subscriptions and read the billed plans.
